To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1·0 and 1·5 µg of ACTH are reliable tests to evaluate ACTH deficiency.
the hypothalamo– pituitary–adrenocortical axis is a complex system and the evaluation of its function should be tailored to the clinical setting, the patient and the available tests.
the insulin tolerance test remains the gold standard for evaluating the HPA axis, but when it is contraindicated the ACTH 1·0 μg test can be used as a reliable alternative.

the comparison of different provocative HPA axis tests, and in particular, the reliability of the 1·0 and 0·5 µg ACTH tests in the evaluation of HPA axis function.
the evaluation of the diagnostic accuracy of the low dose ACTH (LDA) test in comparison with other tests.
the evaluation of the diagnostic accuracy of different provocative tests to assess HPA axis function in patients with hypothalamic–hypophysitis, craniopharyngiomas and pituitary adenomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 1·0-µg ACTH test should not be used as a first-line test in the diagnosis of ACTH deficiency.
the 1·0 and 0·25 µg ACTH tests are not reliable in the assessment of HPA function and should not be used in the clinical practice.
there is no reliable and safe alternative to ITT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we compared different HPA axis tests, and found that the 0.5 μg ACTH test was the best.
the 0·25 µg ACTH stimulation test is a reliable test for the evaluation of HPA axis in patients with suspected ACTH insiciency, and that it is superior to 1·0 and 250 µg tests.
the 1·0 and 0·5 µg ACTH tests are reliable tests for the diagnosis of ACTH insufficiencies, and they are safe in patients with a history of cerebrovascular accidents.

the insulin tolerance test is the gold standard for evaluating the hypothalamic– pituitary–adrenocortical axis in the setting of suspected ACTH insuﬃciency.
